extension.summary: tofa media server: user interface, plus a browsable video source
extension.description:
An unofficial client for the tofa media server (tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Opening Options on a title's page, and starting playback, is quick again whenever the file plays directly. - When a title cannot start because the server is busy or cannot be reached, the message now offers Try again, and when the server cannot convert it fast enough, Lower quality. - Choosing a different subtitle while your server converts a video now shows the one you picked, instead of switching back to one chosen earlier. - A film that belongs to a series, the James Bond films for instance, now lists the rest of that series first under More Like This, including the ones not in your library yet. - The Who's watching? screen is closer to the other tofa apps: a larger lock on protected profiles, a gentle lift and glow on the one you are about to choose, a ring on the profile you are using, and a background tinted in the chosen profile's colour. - A season with only some of its episodes in your library now counts what you have watched against the episodes you can play. - The language lists in Settings now offer the same 42 languages as the other tofa apps, and each Settings page remembers where you were on it. - Skipping forward or back shows the time you will land on, and the bubble leaves as soon as the jump is made. - Smaller touches to match the other tofa apps: quieter format labels on a title's page, the version at the foot of Settings, your server's name without a library count, and Sign Out's confirmation starting on Cancel.
